scope: hosted re-run of the three weakest lanes: bank-statement (round 13 prompts), expense-tracker and timezone (round 15 prompts); one single-lane agent per server
method: One anonymous token minted with GET https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/connect (200, text/html, 8623 bytes, minted anon_2d5f0c11d9f0acc11d8e1ddac2ba8d83) and reused for the whole run. Registered two http entries in mcp.json, https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/bank-statement/t/<token> and https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/expense-tracker/t/<token>, no --header anywhere, each carrying a per-server env block with fresh XDG_DATA_HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME/XDG_CACHE_HOME/XDG_STATE_HOME under the scratch dir. Explicit allowlist of 29 mcp__<server>__<tool> entries read live from tools/list (bank-statement 15, expense-tracker 14). One curl seed before the run: expense_add on /mcp/expense-tracker, EUR 61.50 Adobe Creative Cloud dated 2026-08-07, matching one of the fixture's two Adobe Creative Cloud debits, so reconcile_expenses (b5) has something to reconcile, per r11's method. Client: claude 2.1.261, --model sonnet, --strict-mcp-config, --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 12, one --session-id then five --resume, one per prompt, timeout 240 per prompt, each prompt's raw JSON written to disk before the next ran. Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch, NotebookEdit, Task and TodoWrite disallowed; the working directory was empty. Fixture: remote/fixtures/revolut-main.csv, committed on main, read by the hosted bank_upload {url} shim from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theluckystrike/mcp-servers/main/remote/fixtures/revolut-main.csv (42 data rows, one REVERTED, Spotify x2, Adobe Creative Cloud x2 plus one Adobe Stock, five Coffee Republic rows, three incoming payments, everything else one-off card spend); every total below was independently recomputed with csv.DictReader before the run and matched exactly what the server returned. Clock: 2026-09-05, on a UTC+07 machine.
rubric: 3 = correct, right numbers, no clarification. 2 = correct but needed a second turn, a workaround, or left the user a gap. 1 = partially wrong. 0 = failed.

scenarios.prompt: Here is my bank export at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theluckystrike/mcp-servers/main/remote/fixtures/revolut-main.csv - import it as Main.
scenarios.note: bank_upload {url} fetched 4422 bytes, 43 lines, from raw.githubusercontent.com; statement_import read it by name: 41 imported, 1 REVERTED row skipped and named, Revolut auto-detected, date range 2026-07-28 to 2026-09-03 exactly right. That part is a 3. But the same turn then unprompted set category rules, ran the August summary, ran recurring_detect and reconcile_expenses, and attempted statement_export, none of which b1 asked for - it answered b2 through b6's questions before the user asked them, spending 6 extra tool calls under the same rate-limited token and pre-empting every later turn. Scoped strictly to 'import it as Main', the import itself is right; scoped to what a caller who typed one sentence actually gets back, this is a scope violation, not a wrong answer.

scenarios.note: Because b1 already did this, the model re-checked live rather than trusting memory: accounts_list confirmed 41 transactions still there, category_rules (read path) confirmed 3 rules exactly as asked, free_limit 5. It reported nothing left to do rather than re-running the write and told the user b3-b5 were already answered. Verified live by curl: category_rules read returns {count:3, rules:[spotify/adobe->Software, coffee->Meals], free_limit:5}.

scenarios.note: One fresh statement_summary {group_by: category}: EUR 1,283.73 out over 36 rows, EUR 4,524.99 in kept separate, Software 132.99, Meals 21.30, uncategorised 1,129.44 on 28 rows. Matches an independent csv.DictReader pass over the fixture exactly, and matches r11's identical hosted numbers for the same fixture shape.

recurring_detect now answers on the free tier instead of refusing (the D-R55 guardrail fix): Spotify EUR 9.99 and Adobe Creative Cloud EUR 61.50, both cadence_confirmed false with only 2 occurrences each and annualised null, and free_tier_note names the 3-month/5-charge cap. The model relayed the honest uncertainty verbatim instead of hand-computing and inventing a yearly figure - r11's exact defect (Adobe annualised to about EUR 1,656/year off two charges 14 days apart) did not reproduce.

scenarios.prompt: Which of my expenses have no bank line, and which bank lines have no receipt?
scenarios.note: reconcile_expenses now answers on the free tier instead of refusing (the same guardrail fix): 0 expenses without a bank line (the seeded Adobe EUR 61.50 matched), 33 of 34 bank lines in the free 31-day window without a receipt, and the free_tier_note named exactly which slice of the asked range it covered (2026-08-04 to 2026-09-03 of 2026-07-28 to 2026-09-03) and why the first week was left out. Verified live by curl: bank_debits 34, matched 1, unmatched_bank has exactly 33 entries.

The model did not buy it, relayed the refusal and link, then used the free transactions_list to print the 4 September rows inline (9.99 + 25.00 + 3.60 + 6.40 = EUR 44.99, matching the independent calc) and even hand-typed a CSV block for the user to copy. scenarios.prompt: Log three expenses: 2026-09-01 Figma EUR 45 (software), 2026-09-02 taxi PLN 68 (travel), 2026-09-03 Adobe EUR 22.99 (software).
scenarios.note: Three expense_add calls, one per line, two currencies never mixed. Each reply named the billable default unprompted (no project means billable: false, will not appear in expense_to_invoice unless billable: true is passed) and explained VAT stayed 0 because none was given or stored. No business profile was seeded this round, so unlike r15 there was no default_tax_rate to name; that is a seed difference, not a regression. Verified against a direct expense_list curl: ids 1e6e659c/6d20e77f/f95007d6, amounts and currencies exact.

scenarios.prompt: Give me a summary of September so far, grouped by category.
scenarios.note: One expense_summary. EUR software 67.99 and PLN travel 68.00, correct to the cent. The model relayed the count and offered to pull the bank side in. D-R76 is fixed on the live endpoint: this is the one scenario that changed grade from round 15, exactly where the fix targeted.

scenarios.prompt: Find me a 60 minute meeting slot with Ann and Kenji in the next week that works for all three of us.
scenarios.note: D-R82 holds live: find_meeting_slots ran on the FIRST turn with no question asked, resolving Me from the shared business profile (Europe/Warsaw) and Ann/Kenji from their saved contacts, and the payload's own 'Zones you did not pass' block named all three sources. No slot exists inside standard 09:00-17:00 hours for all three (Warsaw/New York/Tokyo genuinely do not overlap on a 9-5 day), so the tool correctly reported no fit and ranked the three closest compromises. D-R84 also fired server-side: the payload appended 'Searched 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-09 (5 calendar day(s) forward ... weekends skipped)' plus a rollover sentence naming that the search window is past this calendar week's end because the run day is Saturday. Marked down because the model's final answer to the user relayed the free-tier 5-of-7-day cap but DROPPED the D-R84 rollover sentence entirely -- the user was never told 'this week' had already run out when the ask happened on a Saturday. Client-side gap, not a repeat of D-R82 or D-R84 server-side.

defects.title: A single-sentence import request produced a five-tool unrequested cascade covering every later prompt in the round
defects.detail: Asked only to 'import it as Main', the model imported correctly and then, in the same turn, set category rules, ran the August summary, ran recurring_detect and reconcile_expenses, and attempted statement_export - six tool calls the prompt never asked for, on a token metered at 600 calls/hour. This is not a server defect (every tool it called answered correctly, verified live by curl) but a client-side scope problem: agentic sonnet, given the whole allowlist up front and no instruction to wait for the next turn, pre-empted the rest of the conversation. It cost b2 nothing (it re-verified live rather than trusting memory) but it means the round's six prompts are no longer independent measurements of what each individual ask produces - b1 alone did the work of b1 through b5 plus a b6 attempt. Not scored as a 1 or 0 because nothing it did was wrong; scored a 2 because the import-only prompt did not get an import-only answer.
